title: STEM 2
learning_outcomes_intro: After successfully completing the module, students will be able to

items: articulate accurately relationships of differential calculus and kinematics.
reproduce essential concepts of geometrical (ray) optics reliably.
capture basic principles of the paraxial processing model for imaging systems.
understand mathematical modelling of simple dynamical systems.
apply methods for the description of dynamic systems to simple systems.
apply the basic laws of ray optics to the imaging properties of camera lenses.
analyse the effect of varying system parameters and initial conditions on system behaviour.
compare optical imaging in photography / cinematography and computer graphics / computer vision.
evaluate different physics engines in terms of their functionality and simulation fidelity and realism.
Foundations: Basic Calculus, Parametrized Curves in the plane and in three-dimensional space,
Elements of Kinematics
Dynamical Systems: Deterministic Models, Differential Equations
Setting up and Evaluating Models for Example Systems
Project Work: Visualization of the Behaviour of Simple Systems by Means of Web Applications
Foundations of Camera Optics: Paraxial Ray Tracing, Camera Lenses and their cardinal points
Focus, Magnification, Depth of Focus
Comparison: Optical Properties of the Human Eye vs. Camera Optics
Physics Engines
Seminar
none
